mainTopic: The order of offerings (blood, limbs, and parts of חטאת, עולה, אשם and others), and whether אימורים of קדשים קלים that leave the עזרה before זריקה are פסול.
overview: The גמרא asks where the משנה's order comes from: the blood of a חטאת goes before the blood of an עולה, but the limbs of an עולה are burned before the parts of a חטאת. A ברייתא learns this from two פסוקים about the bulls of the לויים, one calling the חטאת 'second' and one naming it first. The גמרא asks why all of the חטאת's blood placements go first, and רבינא and the scholars of ארץ ישראל each give an answer. Next come three open questions about mixed pairs: חטאת blood against עולה limbs, עולה blood against חטאת parts, and עולה blood against אשם blood. Each proof from the משנה is pushed aside. The גמרא then challenges each step of the משנה's order with 'אדרבה' and defends it with 'אפילו הכי'. Along the way, a ברייתא settles that a תודה comes before an איל נזיר. Finally, רבינא בר שילא rules that אימורים of קדשים קלים that leave the עזרה before the blood is sprinkled are פסול. The גמרא supports this from the משנה, tests a proof from רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, and begins comparing it to a dispute between תנאים that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where does the משנה's order of offerings come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rule about the order of the חטאת and the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the source of the rule in the משנה. This question sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a split order. The blood of the חטאת comes before the blood of the עולה. But the limbs of the עולה are burned before the parts of the חטאת. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this mixed order.

steps.title: The 'second bull' verse: the חטאת does not come first in everything
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא points out that the extra words 'a second bull for a חטאת' must teach that the חטאת does not come before every part of the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: 'And a second young bull you shall take for a sin offering.' If this comes to teach that there are two bulls, it already says, 'Offer the one as a sin offering and the one as a burnt offering.' So why does the verse say 'a second young bull for a sin offering'? Because you might have thought the sin offering comes before all the rites of the burnt offering. So the verse says 'a second young bull for a sin offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק about the bulls brought when the לויים were consecrated. It asks why the חטאת is called the 'second' bull, since we already know there are two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another פסוק already tells us there are two bulls, so the word 'second' cannot just be counting. The extra word must teach something new. In some way the חטאת comes after the עולה, so it does not come first in every part of the service.

steps.title: The other verse: the עולה does not come first in everything
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא balances things. Since the other פסוק lists the חטאת first, the עולה cannot come first in everything either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it only said 'a second bull,' you might think the burnt offering comes before the sin offering in all its rites. So the verse says, 'Offer the one as a sin offering and the one as a burnt offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now warns against going too far the other way. The second פסוק names the חטאת first, so the חטאת must come first in some part of the service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק makes the חטאת 'second.' The other names it first. So neither offering can come first in everything. This sets up the split that comes in the next step.

steps.title: The resolution: חטאת blood first, עולה limbs first
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא settles the two פסוקים. The blood of the חטאת goes first because it brings atonement. The limbs of the עולה are burned first.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? The blood of the sin offering comes before the blood of the burnt offering, because it brings atonement. The limbs of the burnt offering come before the parts of the sin offering, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows how both פסוקים can be true. Each offering comes first in a different part of the service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood stage goes to the חטאת first, because its blood brings atonement. The burning stage goes to the עולה first, which fits the חטאת being called 'second.' This matches the משנה exactly.

steps.whatToRemember: In the blood stage the חטאת goes first, because it brings atonement. In the burning stage the עולה goes first, because the חטאת is called 'second.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the משנה's split order, and the next step builds directly on its reason ('because it brings atonement').

steps.title: If atonement is the reason, only the first placement should go first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reason. Only the first placement of the חטאת's blood brings atonement, so why should all its placements come before the עולה's blood?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let the first placement, which brings atonement, come first, and those others should not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the reason the ברייתא gave. If the חטאת goes first only because it brings atonement, that should apply only to its first placement of blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חטאת's blood is put on the מזבח in several placements. Only the first one does the work of atonement. So the reason 'because it brings atonement' seems to cover only that first placement. The later ones should not have to come before the עולה's blood.

steps.title: רבינא: the verse is about the Levites' sin offering
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the פסוק is about the חטאת of the לויים. That חטאת is like an עולה, yet the Torah still says it comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The פסוק here is talking about the חטאת of the לויים. Even though it is like an עולה, the Torah says it should come first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question from step 5. He shows that the Torah puts a חטאת first even when the reason of atonement does not fully apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that only the first placement of blood brings atonement, so why should all the placements come first? רבינא points to the חטאת of the לויים. It is like an עולה because it was not for a sin, and the Torah still put it first. So the order does not depend on each placement bringing atonement.

steps.title: The West: once he begins the placements, he finishes
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of ארץ ישראל give a second answer. Once the כהן has started placing the חטאת's blood, he finishes all the placements.

steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the question from step 5. Once the כהן starts the חטאת's blood placements, he does not stop in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer agrees that only the first placement brings atonement. But that first placement already puts the חטאת ahead, and it makes sense to finish the job before moving on to the עולה.

steps.title: Which comes first: sin offering blood or burnt offering limbs?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: if we have the blood of a חטאת and the limbs of an עולה, which is offered first?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: The blood of a חטאת and the limbs of an עולה, which comes first? Does the blood of the חטאת come first because it brings atonement? Or do the limbs of the עולה come first because they are burned completely on the fire?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It compares two different parts of the offerings: the חטאת's blood and the עולה's limbs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has a good reason. The חטאת's blood brings atonement. The עולה's limbs go entirely to the מזבח's fire, with nothing eaten by people. The question is which reason wins.

steps.title: A proof from the first part of the mishna
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from the משנה that the חטאת's blood comes first only against the עולה's blood, not against its limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The blood of a חטאת comes before the blood of an עולה. It comes first only before the עולה's blood, but not before the עולה's limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question by reading the exact words of the משנה closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the חטאת's blood comes before the עולה's blood. The extra precision of 'blood' suggests that against the עולה's limbs, the חטאת's blood does not come first. So the limbs would win.

steps.title: The end of the mishna points the other way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Reading the end of the משנה the same way gives the opposite result, so we cannot learn anything from the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, look at the end of the משנה: The limbs of an עולה come before the fats of a חטאת. They come first only before the חטאת's fats, but not before the חטאת's blood! So we cannot learn anything from this משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the end of the משנה, read the same way, proves the opposite. So the משנה does not answer the question at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beginning of the משנה suggests the limbs win. The end of the משנה suggests the חטאת's blood wins. Since the two readings cancel each other out, the question stays open.

steps.title: Blood of an עולה versus fat parts of a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which comes first: putting the blood of an עולה on the מזבח, or burning the אימורים of a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if there is blood of an עולה and fat parts of a חטאת, which goes first? Maybe the עולה's blood goes first, because it comes from an offering that is burned completely. Or maybe the חטאת's fat parts go first, because they come from an offering that brings atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. It is the reverse of the question in Step 8: now we have the עולה's blood and the חטאת's fat parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has its own strong point. The עולה is כליל, burned completely on the מזבח. The חטאת is מכפר, it brings atonement. The question is which of these two strengths decides the order when the עולה brings its blood and the חטאת brings only its fat parts.

steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to infer from the משנה that only the חטאת's blood beats the עולה's blood, but the חטאת's fat parts do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the משנה says the blood of a חטאת comes before the blood of an עולה. That means only the חטאת's blood comes first, not the חטאת's fat parts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question by reading the opening line of the משנה closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה specifically says "the blood of a חטאת" comes before the עולה's blood. The גמרא reads that as a limit: only the blood has that power. So the חטאת's fat parts would not come before the עולה's blood.

keyTerms.meaning: It is the one that comes first (only it)

steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה, read the same way, gives the opposite result. So the משנה cannot settle the question.

steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the משנה says "the limbs of an עולה" come before the חטאת's fat parts. Read as a limit, that means the עולה's blood would not come before the חטאת's fat parts. The two readings of the משנה contradict each other, so neither one proves anything.

but the blood of the olah does not!
Rather, from this nothing can be learned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, מִסֵּיפָא: אֵיבְרֵי עוֹלָה קוֹדְמִין לְאֵימוּרֵי חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 12, just like Step 10 rejected Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely. The question of Step 11 stays unanswered.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Reading the first line of the משנה as a limit is matched by reading the last line as a limit, and the two give opposite results.

steps.title: Blood of an עולה versus blood of an אשם
steps.stepSummary: A new question: which blood goes on the מזבח first, the עולה's or the אשם's?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if there is blood of an עולה and blood of an אשם, which goes first? Maybe the עולה's blood goes first, because the עולה is burned completely. Or maybe the אשם's blood goes first, because it brings atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. This time it is blood against blood, but the חטאת is replaced with an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said the חטאת's blood beats the עולה's blood, because the חטאת brings atonement. An אשם also brings atonement, so maybe it beats the עולה too. Or maybe the עולה being כליל wins here, and the חטאת only came first because of something special about the חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A guilt offering, which also brings atonement
Or perhaps

phrases.aramaic: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: דַּם עוֹלָה וְדַם אָשָׁם,
phrases.english: A question was asked of them: blood of an olah and blood of an asham,
which of them comes first?

phrases.aramaic: דַּם עוֹלָה קוֹדֵם – דְּקָאָתֵי מִכֹּחַ כָּלִיל;
phrases.english: Does the blood of the olah come first, since it comes from the strength of an offering burned whole;
or perhaps the blood of the asham comes first,
since it brings atonement?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets ("since it comes from the strength of") and some don't. Either way, the reason is that the אשם brings atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: דַּם עוֹלָה וְדַם אָשָׁם, אֵיזֶה מֵהֶן קוֹדֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 13 left the earlier question unresolved, the גמרא asks about another pair of offerings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether atonement (מכפר) gives the אשם's blood priority over the עולה's blood, as it does for the חטאת, or whether the עולה being כליל wins.

steps.title: A proof from the line about the חטאת's blood
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the חטאת's blood comes before the עולה's blood. That suggests the אשם's blood does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the blood of a חטאת comes before the blood of an עולה. But the blood of an אשם does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from Step 14 using the משנה. Since the משנה named only the חטאת's blood as coming before the עולה's blood, the אשם's blood seems not to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a proof based on what the משנה left out. If the אשם's blood also beat the עולה's blood, why did the משנה mention only the חטאת? So the גמרא suggests that the עולה's blood goes before the אשם's blood. The next step rejects this proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood: here, putting the blood on the מזבח
Comes first, goes before
A guilt offering

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The blood of a sin offering comes before the blood of a burnt offering.
But the blood of a guilt offering does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דַּם חַטָּאת קוֹדֵם לְדַם עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first attempt to answer the question asked in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the עולה's blood goes on the מזבח before the אשם's blood.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's line 'דם חטאת קודם לדם עולה', read as leaving out the אשם on purpose.

steps.title: The משנה only said חטאת to match its second half
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The משנה really should have said אשם, but it chose חטאת because of its next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the משנה should have taught 'the blood of an אשם.' But since it wanted to teach the next part, 'the limbs of an עולה come before the fat parts of a חטאת,' it used חטאת here too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says the word חטאת in the first line was not chosen on purpose. It was chosen only to match the second line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה had said 'the אשם's blood beats the עולה's blood,' we would know the חטאת's blood does too, since the חטאת beats the אשם. That would have been the better way to teach it. The משנה said חטאת only so its two lines would match, so nothing can be proven from it.

keyTerms.meaning: By right; really it should have been
Since, because of: the משנה said one thing to match another
The later part of the משנה
The limbs of the עולה, which are burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves. The first line is about blood (חטאת's blood before עולה's blood). The second line is the reverse, about burning (the עולה's limbs before the חטאת's fat parts).

phrases.aramaic: בְּדִין הוּא דְּאִיבְּעִי לְמִיתְנֵי דַּם אָשָׁם;
phrases.english: By right, it should have taught 'the blood of a guilt offering';
but since it wanted to teach the later part:
'The limbs of a burnt offering come before the fat parts of a sin offering' —

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּדִין הוּא דְּאִיבְּעִי לְמִיתְנֵי דַּם אָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 15 by explaining the משנה's choice of words.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the first line of the משנה is cancelled. The question itself is still open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word חטאת in the first line was used only to match the second line. It does not mean the אשם was left out on purpose.

steps.title: Why the second half had to say חטאת
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had said the עולה's limbs beat the אשם's fat parts, we would think they do not beat the holier חטאת. So the second half had to say חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if it had taught 'before the fat parts of an אשם,' I would have thought that the limbs beat only the אשם's fat parts, but not the חטאת's fat parts. That is why it taught חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its rejection by explaining why the second line really needed the word חטאת. That line then forced the first line to say חטאת as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second line, the עולה is the one that wins. To teach the biggest lesson, the משנה names the strongest offering the עולה beats, which is the חטאת, since it is holier than the אשם. If it had said אשם, we might have thought the עולה does not beat the חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
The fat parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח
Because of this, that is why

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה uses חטאת in both lines. In the second line the word is needed. In the first line it is only there to match, so we cannot prove from it that the אשם's blood comes after the עולה's blood.

phrases.english: because if it had taught 'the fat parts of a guilt offering,'
I would have said:
it is only the guilt offering's fat parts that they come before,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the limbs of the עולה.

phrases.english: but they do not come before the sin offering's fat parts —
Because of this, it taught 'sin offering.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי תְּנָא לְאֵימוּרֵי אָשָׁם, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the claim in Step 16 that the second line needed the word חטאת. This completes the rejection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה's wording: the second line names the strongest case so we cannot read it too narrowly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the משנה had said אשם, we would think the עולה's limbs do not come before the holier חטאת's fat parts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second line had to say חטאת, and the first line said חטאת only to match it.

steps.title: A new proof from 'חטאת comes before אשם'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a חטאת comes before an אשם. That suggests an עולה does not, and the גמרא asks whether this is talking about blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a חטאת comes before an אשם. It is only the חטאת that comes before the אשם, but not an עולה. Is this not talking about the blood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second proof from a different line of the משנה. If that line is about blood, it would show that the עולה's blood does not come before the אשם's blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the חטאת beats the אשם and did not say the עולה does. The גמרא suggests this line is about putting the blood on the מזבח. If so, the אשם's blood would go before the עולה's blood, which is the opposite of the first attempt in Step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: What, is it not...? (a question that suggests a proof)
It comes before it

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A sin offering comes before a guilt offering —
it is only the sin offering that comes before the guilt offering,
but a burnt offering does not.
What, is it not talking about the blood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected in Steps 16 and 17, this step offers a new proof for the question from Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the אשם's blood goes on the מזבח before the עולה's blood.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's line 'חטאת קודמת לאשם', which names only the חטאת and not the עולה as coming before the אשם, assuming it is about blood.

steps.title: No, the line is about the fat parts, not the blood
steps.stepSummary: The proof from step 18 is pushed off. The משנה's line about חטאת before אשם is talking about the אימורים, not the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is talking about the fat parts that get burned on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question from step 18. That line of the משנה is not about blood at all, so it proves nothing about whose blood goes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 tried to learn from the משנה that an עולה's blood does not come before an אשם's blood. If the line is really about the אימורים, it tells us nothing about blood. So the question about blood stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: The fat parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: No; it is about the sacrificial portions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question at the end of step 18 and rejects its proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה about the order of blood
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה was talking about blood, but it is talking about the אימורים.

steps.title: The משנה's own wording supports this
steps.stepSummary: The wording 'because its blood is placed' shows that blood is the reason for the order, not the thing being ordered. So the subject must be the אימורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact, because it says 'because its blood is placed.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer from step 19 with the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the חטאת comes first 'because its blood is placed' on the four corners. If the משנה were ordering the blood, it would just describe the blood. Using blood as the reason shows that something else is being put in order, and that is the אימורים.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact (it supports this)
Learn from this (the point is proven)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's line about חטאת before אשם is about the אימורים, so the question of the עולה's blood against the אשם's blood is not settled here.

phrases.english: It is also precise,
as it teaches, 'because its blood is placed.'
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 19 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's line is about the אימורים

steps.title: Shouldn't the guilt offering come before the sin offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule that a חטאת comes before an אשם. The אשם has a fixed minimum value, so maybe it should come first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a חטאת comes before an אשם. On the contrary, the אשם should come first, because it has a fixed value!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins going through the order in the משנה. It challenges the first pair, חטאת against אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם must be worth at least a fixed amount, but a חטאת has no minimum price. That seems to make the אשם more important, which goes against the משנה's order.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
A fixed amount (a minimum value)

phrases.english: A sin offering precedes, etc.
On the contrary, the guilt offering should precede,
since it has a fixed value!
phrases.notes: The אשם must be worth at least two shekels (ויקרא 5:15).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a חטאת comes before an אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The אשם has a fixed minimum value, which seems to give it more importance.

steps.title: More blood on the altar wins
steps.stepSummary: The חטאת's blood is put on the מזבח more times, and that counts for more than the אשם's fixed value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, having more blood placements on the מזבח is more important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps the משנה's order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא agrees that the אשם has a fixed value. Still, the חטאת's blood goes on all four corners of the מזבח, and that extra service on the מזבח outweighs the fixed value.

keyTerms.meaning: Even so
More placements of blood on the מזבח
Is better, counts for more

phrases.english: Even so,
more placements on the altar is preferable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing two advantages and deciding which counts for more
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אשם's fixed value should give it first place.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חטאת's extra blood placements on the מזבח count for more, so the חטאת comes first.

steps.title: Shouldn't the thanks offering and nazirite's ram come first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that an אשם comes before a תודה and an איל נזיר, since those two come with loaves of bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: an אשם comes before a תודה. On the contrary, the תודה and the איל נזיר should come first, because they need loaves of bread!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the next pair in the משנה's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה and an איל נזיר are brought together with bread, and an אשם is not. That extra part seems to make them more important.

keyTerms.meaning: A thanks offering
The ram a נזיר brings when he finishes his נזירות
They need loaves of bread brought with them

phrases.english: A guilt offering precedes a thanks offering, etc.
On the contrary, the thanks offering and nazirite's ram should precede,
since they require bread!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה, using the same 'on the contrary' pattern.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that an אשם comes before a תודה and an איל נזיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bread brought with the תודה and איל נזיר seems to make them more important.

steps.title: Most holy offerings win
steps.stepSummary: The אשם is one of the קדשי קדשים, and that counts for more than the bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, offerings of the most holy kind are more important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps the משנה's order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא agrees that the תודה and איל נזיר have the bread. Still, the אשם belongs to the holiest group of קרבנות, and the תודה and איל נזיר are only קדשים קלים. Its higher level of holiness decides the order.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the most holy kind

phrases.english: Even so,
offerings of the most sacred order are preferable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing two advantages and deciding which counts for more
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bread should give the תודה and איל נזיר first place.
steps.terutzMaskana: Being קדשי קדשים counts for more, so the אשם comes first.

steps.title: Shouldn't peace offerings come first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that a תודה and an איל נזיר come before שלמים, since the community also brings שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a תודה and an איל נזיר come before שלמים. On the contrary, שלמים should come first, because they are brought by the community as well as by one person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last pair in this part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים are brought both by the whole community and by one person. A תודה and an איל נזיר are only brought by one person. That wider use seems to make שלמים more important.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings
The community
A single person

phrases.english: A thanks offering and nazirite's ram, etc.
On the contrary, peace offerings should precede,
since they exist for the community as for the individual!
phrases.notes: The community brings שלמים on שבועות, but there is no communal תודה or איל נזיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה, using the same 'on the contrary' pattern.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a תודה and an איל נזיר come before שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שלמים are also brought by the community, which seems to make them more important.

steps.title: Eaten for only one day wins
steps.stepSummary: The תודה and איל נזיר may be eaten for only one day, and that counts for more than the community also bringing שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, offerings that are eaten for only one day are more important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps the משנה's order. The run of 'on the contrary' challenges pauses here for a side question (step 27) and picks up again in step 29.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary שלמים may be eaten for two days and a night. The תודה and איל נזיר have a shorter time to be eaten, which shows they are stricter, and that counts for more than the community also bringing שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Eaten for only one day (and the night after it)

steps.whatToRemember: Each time, the גמרא names a reason the other קרבן might come first. Each time it answers 'אפילו הכי': the משנה's reason counts for more, so the משנה's order stands.

phrases.english: Even so,
those eaten for one day are preferable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, נֶאֱכָלִין לְיוֹם אֶחָד עֲדִיפִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing two advantages and deciding which counts for more
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being brought by the community too should give שלמים first place.
steps.terutzMaskana: Having only one day to be eaten counts for more, so the תודה and איל נזיר come first.

steps.title: Thanks offering or nazirite's ram: which comes first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which comes first, a תודה or an איל נזיר, and gives a reason for each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if there is a תודה and an איל נזיר, which one comes first? Maybe the תודה comes first, because it needs four kinds of bread. Or maybe the איל נזיר comes first, because other offerings' blood comes along with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה said that both of these come before שלמים. Now the גמרא asks which of the two comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has its own strong point. The תודה has more kinds of bread. The איל נזיר comes as part of a set, together with the נזיר's עולה and חטאת, whose blood also goes on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked (a real open question)
Thanks offering
The ram a נזיר brings at the end of his נזירות
Or perhaps
Other blood, meaning other offerings brought with it

phrases.english: A question was asked:
A thanks offering and a nazirite's ram:
Which of them comes first?
Does the thanks offering come first,
since it needs four kinds of bread?
Or perhaps the nazirite's ram comes first,
since other offerings' blood comes with it?
phrases.notes: A נזיר also brings an עולה and a חטאת along with his ram.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from comparing these two offerings with שלמים to comparing them with each other.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which comes first, a תודה or an איל נזיר?

steps.title: A ברייתא answers: the thanks offering comes first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the תודה comes first because it has four kinds of bread, while the איל נזיר has only two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: this one comes before that one, because this one needs four kinds of bread, and that one needs only two kinds of bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that answers the question directly: the תודה comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא decides by the amount of bread: four kinds beats two. The other blood that comes with the איל נזיר does not tip the balance.

keyTerms.meaning: Kinds of bread

phrases.english: Come and hear:
This one comes before that one,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the תודה, and 'that one' is the איל נזיר.

phrases.english: because this one needs four kinds of bread,

phrases.aramaic: וְזוֹ אֵינָהּ טְעוּנָה אֶלָּא שְׁנֵי מִינֵי לֶחֶם.
phrases.english: and that one needs only two kinds of bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תודה comes first because of its four kinds of bread.

steps.title: Shouldn't the firstborn come before peace offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule that שלמים come before a בכור. A בכור is holy from birth and is eaten only by כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And שלמים come before a בכור.' On the contrary, the בכור should come first! It is holy from the womb, and it is eaten only by כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה and argues that the order should be the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור has two strong points. Its holiness comes on its own at birth, and only כהנים may eat it. שלמים, on the other hand, are eaten by anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn animal, given to a כהן
On the contrary
Its holiness comes from the womb (from birth)
Peace offerings

phrases.english: 'And peace offerings come before a firstborn, etc.'
On the contrary, the firstborn should come first,
since it is holy from the womb,
and it is eaten by the priests!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the pattern of steps 21 to 26, challenging the next rule in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that שלמים come before a בכור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The בכור has holiness from birth and is eaten only by כהנים, so it seems more important.

steps.title: Extra מצוות count for more
steps.stepSummary: Even so, the extra מצוות done with שלמים count for more than the בכור's strong points.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, extra מצוות count for more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the משנה's order. The extra מצוות of שלמים win.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed what שלמים have that a בכור does not: more placements of blood, סמיכה, נסכים, and תנופה. All these extra actions count for more than holiness from birth and being eaten only by כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Even so
Extra מצוות
Are more important, count for more

phrases.english: Even so,

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בכור's holiness from birth and its being eaten by כהנים should put it first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra מצוות of שלמים count for more, so שלמים come first.

steps.title: Shouldn't the animal tithe come before the firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that a בכור comes before מעשר. מעשר can make the animals before and after it holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'The בכור comes first.' On the contrary, מעשר should come first! It makes holy the animal before it and the animal after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the next rule in the משנה, saying מעשר seems stronger than a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר בהמה has a special power. If someone mistakenly calls the ninth or eleventh animal 'tenth,' that animal also becomes holy. So its holiness seems to reach further than a בכור's.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal tithe (every tenth animal)
Makes holy the animal before it and after it

phrases.english: 'The firstborn comes first, etc.'
On the contrary, the tithe should come first,
since it makes holy the one before it and the one after it!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעשר can make even neighboring animals holy, so it seems to have stronger holiness.

steps.title: Holiness from birth counts for more
steps.stepSummary: Even so, the בכור's holiness from birth counts for more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, holiness from the womb counts for more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the משנה's order. The בכור's holiness from birth wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור becomes holy all by itself the moment it is born. מעשר becomes holy only when a person counts and calls it 'tenth.' Holiness that comes on its own counts for more than holiness that spreads to the neighboring animals.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness from the womb

steps.terutzMaskana: Holiness from birth counts for more, so the בכור comes first.

steps.title: Shouldn't bird offerings come before the animal tithe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that מעשר comes before birds. Bird offerings are קדשי קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'מעשר comes before birds.' On the contrary, birds should come first, since they are קדשי קדשים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last rule in this part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bird offerings, whether an עולה or a חטאת, are קדשי קדשים, the highest level of holiness. מעשר is only קדשים קלים. So it seems the birds should win.

keyTerms.meaning: Bird offerings
Offerings of the highest holiness

phrases.english: 'The tithe comes before birds, etc.'
On the contrary, birds should come first,
since they are offerings of the highest holiness!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to challenge the next rule in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that מעשר comes before bird offerings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Birds are קדשי קדשים while מעשר is not, so birds seem more important.

steps.title: Being an animal offering counts for more
steps.stepSummary: Even so, being a slaughtered animal offering counts for more than the birds' higher level of holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, being a kind of slaughtered offering counts for more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the משנה's order: מעשר, an animal that is slaughtered, comes before birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Birds are not slaughtered; their necks are pinched (מליקה). An animal that is properly slaughtered as a זבח is a more important kind of offering. That counts for more than the birds being קדשי קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of slaughtered animal offering
Counts for more

steps.whatToRemember: In this whole section, the גמרא keeps saying 'אדרבה' to challenge the משנה's order, and then 'אפילו הכי' to defend it. Each time, the factor the משנה gave is said to outweigh the other side's point. The full order is: extra מצוות beat the בכור, holiness from birth beats מעשר, and being an animal זבח beats birds.

phrases.english: Even so,
being a kind of slaughtered offering counts for more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 33 and closes this run of challenges.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Birds, being קדשי קדשים, should come before מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Being a slaughtered animal offering counts for more, so מעשר comes first.

steps.title: Altar portions that leave before the blood is sprinkled are disqualified
steps.stepSummary: רבינא בר שילא rules that אימורים of קדשים קלים that leave the עזרה before זריקת הדם become פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא בר שילא says: the altar portions of offerings of lesser holiness that left the courtyard before the blood was sprinkled are disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens: רבינא בר שילא gives a rule about the altar portions of lighter offerings that leave the עזרה too early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשים קלים may normally be taken outside the עזרה for eating. But the אימורים are never taken out; they are burned on the מזבח. רבינא בר שילא teaches that even before זריקה, leaving the עזרה already makes them פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: The fats and parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח
Offerings of lesser holiness, like שלמים and מעשר
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
Something holy that left its required area, which makes it פסול

phrases.english: Ravina bar Sheila says:
The altar portions of offerings of lesser holiness
that went out before the sprinkling of the blood
phrases.notes: Went out of the עזרה, the Temple courtyard.

phrases.english: are disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of which offering comes first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אימורים of קדשים קלים that leave the עזרה before זריקת הדם are פסול.

steps.title: Our משנה hints at the same rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says our משנה also teaches this. It calls the blood and אימורים of מעשר 'קדשי קדשים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא also taught it: because it is a slaughtered offering, and it has parts that are most holy, its blood and its altar portions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the line in our משנה about why מעשר comes before birds. It says this line supports רבינא בר שילא. The next steps explain how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says מעשר has two 'most holy' parts, its blood and its אימורים, even though מעשר is קדשים קלים. The גמרא will show that this wording hides רבינא בר שילא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And our Tanna also taught it.' A source from the משנה backs up a statement
A slaughtered animal offering
Offerings or parts of the highest holiness

phrases.english: And our Tanna also taught it:
because it is a slaughtered offering,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's reason why מעשר comes before bird offerings (see step 34).

phrases.english: and it has parts that are most holy:
its blood and its altar portions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from the משנה for the statement in step 35.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא בר שילא's rule that אימורים are disqualified by leaving before זריקה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's words 'ישנו קדשי קדשים, דמיו ואימורין' about מעשר.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention the blood?
steps.stepSummary: Birds have blood too, so blood is not a real advantage over birds. The משנה must mention blood to compare the אימורים to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense to mention the altar portions, since birds don't have them. But birds do have blood! Rather, the משנה must be teaching us that the altar portions are like the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the משנה proves the rule. Blood is not an advantage over birds, so it must be mentioned for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is listing reasons why מעשר is better than birds. אימורים fit that list, because birds have none. Blood does not fit, because birds have blood too. So blood is mentioned to make a comparison: the אימורים share the status of the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It makes sense regarding…' Accepts one point before raising a difficulty about another
Bird offerings
'It is teaching us.' Points to the new lesson hidden in the wording

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is attacking the משנה. It is asking 'why mention blood?' only to discover what the משנה is quietly teaching.

phrases.english: It makes sense regarding the altar portions:
birds don't have them;
but blood, at least, birds do have!
Rather, is it not teaching us:
that the altar portions are like its blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה quoted in step 36 supports רבינא בר שילא.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה is comparing the אימורים to the blood.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Mentioning blood is pointless as an advantage over birds, so it must be there for a comparison.

steps.title: Altar portions are like the blood: disqualified by leaving
steps.stepSummary: The blood and the אימורים are compared. Both are 'most holy' before זריקה, and both become פסול if they leave the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the blood is called most holy before it is sprinkled, so the altar portions are called most holy before the sprinkling. And just as the blood is disqualified by leaving, so the altar portions are disqualified by leaving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. The comparison to blood shows that אימורים before זריקה are disqualified by leaving, just like רבינא בר שילא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood matters only before it is sprinkled. So the משנה is calling the אימורים 'קדשי קדשים' at that same stage, before זריקה. Blood that leaves the עזרה is פסול, and the comparison carries that rule over to the אימורים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Just as… so too…' Carries a rule over from one item to another
Becomes disqualified

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה groups the blood and the אימורים of מעשר together. So the אימורים, like the blood, are treated as most holy before זריקה and become פסול if they leave the עזרה. This backs up רבינא בר שילא.

phrases.english: Just as its blood is before sprinkling,
so too the altar portions are before sprinkling,
and it calls them most holy;
and just as its blood is disqualified by leaving,
so too the altar portions are disqualified by leaving.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה supports רבינא בר שילא: אימורים of קדשים קלים that leave the עזרה before זריקה are פסול, just like the blood.

steps.title: A possible support from the dispute about meat that left early
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a dispute supports רבינא בר שילא. The dispute is between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, about the meat of קדשים קלים that left before זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports him: about meat of offerings of lesser holiness that left before the blood was sprinkled, רבי יוחנן says it is fit, and ריש לקיש says it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second possible proof for רבינא בר שילא, using a dispute among אמוראים. How exactly it supports him is worked out in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the case is the meat, the part eaten by people, not the אימורים. רבי יוחנן says meat that left before זריקה is still כשר. ריש לקיש says it is פסול. The גמרא wants to see whether this dispute connects to רבינא בר שילא's rule about the אימורים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let us say this supports him.' Suggests a proof that may still be pushed aside
The meat of an offering, eaten by people
Fit, valid

the meat of offerings of lesser holiness
that went out before the sprinkling of the blood:

Reish Lakish says: it is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה, the גמרא tries a second support for רבינא בר שילא.

steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about meat of קדשים קלים that left before זריקה.

steps.title: The two opinions about meat that left before זריקה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the meat stays כשר because it will go out of the עזרה eventually anyway. ריש לקיש says it is פסול because its time to go out has not come yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: it is fit, since in the end it will go out anyway. ריש לקיש says: it is unfit, since its time to go out has not yet arrived.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the details of the dispute it mentioned in the last step. This is the setup for the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat of קדשים קלים may be eaten outside the עזרה, but only after the blood is thrown. רבי יוחנן looks at where the meat ends up, so leaving early does no harm. ריש לקיש looks at timing: before זריקה the meat still belongs inside, so leaving makes it פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: fit, valid
unfit, disqualified
since it will eventually go out

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree the meat may go out after זריקה. They argue only about meat that went out too early, before the blood was thrown.

steps.title: They only argue about meat, so everyone agrees about אימורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that the dispute is only about meat. About אימורים, everyone (even רבי יוחנן) would agree they become פסול, which supports רבינא בר שילא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only argue about meat, but about אימורים they do not argue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof: since they argue only about meat, about אימורים all agree they become פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's reason, 'it will go out in the end,' fits only meat. אימורים are burned on the מזבח and never go out. So it seems that even רבי יוחנן would make אימורים פסול, exactly as רבינא בר שילא ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: they only argue up to here, meaning only in this case

the meat that is eaten

steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute is limited to meat, which implies everyone agrees that אימורים become פסול.

steps.title: They argue about אימורים too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about אימורים as well. They mention meat only to show how strict ריש לקיש is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true for אימורים: they argue there too. They argue about meat only to show you how far ריש לקיש goes: even meat, which will go out in the end, he says is פסול because its time to go out has not yet arrived.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The dispute is not limited to meat, so nothing here supports רבינא בר שילא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat is the strongest case for being כשר, since it really is meant to go out. If ריש לקיש makes even meat פסול, his view is clearly strict. So the case was picked to show ריש לקיש's strength, and רבי יוחנן may still call אימורים כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: the same is true
to show you how far his view goes
also

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש does not prove רבינא בר שילא's rule. They may argue about אימורים too.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא: a case may be chosen to show the strength of one opinion, so we cannot assume the dispute stops there.

phrases.english: The same is true: they argue about the אימורים too;
and the reason they argue about meat

since even about meat, which will go out in the end,

steps.title: Is this the same as an older dispute between תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to suggest that this question matches a dispute between תנאים about אימורים of קדשים קלים that left before זריקה. It starts with רבי אליעזר, who says there is no מעילה with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is like a dispute between תנאים? About אימורים of קדשים קלים that went out before the blood was thrown, רבי אליעזר says: one is not liable for מעילה with them,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new suggestion and starts quoting a ברייתא. This is a setup line; the rest of the dispute continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to see if older תנאים already argued about the same issue: what happens to אימורים that left the עזרה before זריקה. For now we only have רבי אליעזר's view, that there is no מעילה with them. The other side of the dispute and the comparison come next.
